tech.why: Bottom of TRL 4: imec 2T0C PBTI was ~1 yr vs 5-yr target (IEDM 2021), the 5-yr/95C result is a 2025 lab abstract, and IWO retention drops to ~300 ms at 85C; no foundry runs an oxide module.

capital.why: T2: dedicated IGZO/In2O3 BEOL tools ($4-10M) plus ~$10-30M module qualification at SkyWater before any license revenue.

ttr.why: 48 months (18-24 mo module development + 12-18 mo PBTI/retention qual), past the 36-month hard ceiling.

usmfg.why: Needs an oxide-semiconductor module that does not exist at SkyWater Bloomington or Fab 25 (no announcement found 2026-11).

margin.why: IP royalties run ~85%, but corrected blended margin is 65-85% because early revenue is NRE and the foundry keeps the wafer adder.

moat.why: University IWO/In2O3 licenses are available, but SEL's dominant oxide-semiconductor estate is an FTO gate; US12191135 shows active patenting by others.

competition.why: No commercial oxide-eDRAM IP vendor on a U.S. 200mm line, but Weebit ReRAM (S130) and RAAAM-style Si gain cells (C-32) serve the same SRAM-limited buyer.

regulatory.why: No export control on the IP itself; defense ASIC customers bring ITAR handling that is manageable.

cycle.why: Priced against on-die SRAM/ReRAM, not DDR5; only exposure is edge-AI ASIC design starts slowing if AI capex drops (the glut trigger).

founder.why: Card: needs a device/process CTO and a SkyWater JDA; process-module development is far beyond <$50k and a day job.

scores.one_line_view: A process-module science project with $15-40M and 48 months to first revenue to win small 130nm royalties, while C-32 serves the same buyer with no new module: pass.

tech.why: HZO 1T1C works (1Mb array, 1e11 cycles, IEDM 2023) but trails PZT's 1e13-1e14 cycles and 10 yr at 125C; Sandia MESA circuitry is still a planned follow-on (2026-05).

capital.why: T2: ~$10-30M for a SkyWater HZO module, product design and QML screening.

ttr.why: 54 months to first industrial/eval sales; QML-V adds 1-2 years for the space buyer.

usmfg.why: No HZO module at SkyWater S130 or Fab 25; Sandia MESA is a trusted DOE fab with limited outside access, not an open foundry.

margin.why: Card 50-65% at hi-rel ASPs; device model $814/GB vs PZT F-RAM street ~$8,192/GB leaves headroom, but low volume against Infineon pricing.

moat.why: Sandia HZO licensing is unconfirmed (01_LANDSCAPE s0 #12), and RAMXEED and CEA-Leti are pursuing the same HZO density axis; QML lock-in is 5+ years away.

competition.why: Infineon ships QML-V 2Mb F-RAM with U.S.-fabbed die (TI Dallas DMOS6); Everspin Toggle (Chandler AZ) and Honeywell trusted MRAM already serve space.

regulatory.why: Rad-hard variants fall under EAR 3A001.a.1/ITAR handling; manageable for a domestic defense buyer.

cycle.why: Mb-class rad-hard NVM is priced on reliability and supply security; a DDR5 glut is irrelevant.

founder.why: Needs a memory designer, a reliability engineer and $10-30M; card rates founder-doable 'no'.

scores.one_line_view: Optane-style capital burn for a third-source slot in a hundreds-of-$M niche where Infineon already ships U.S.-fabbed QML-V F-RAM and HZO still trails PZT on endurance and hot retention.

tech.why: Devices switch at 600C for >60 h (Nature Electronics 2024) and kB arrays are only a preprint (arXiv 2506.05452); the 500C SiC periphery barely exists and drive is ~10-15 V.

capital.why: Realistic path is STTR Phase I (~$323k) plus Phase II (~$2.15M) and high-temperature packaging before a paid eval part, which is T2 money even if non-dilutive.

ttr.why: First paid eval-part sale at 36-48 months (corrected 42); AF254-D0806 and DV017 topics are both closed now.

usmfg.why: Prototyping at Penn Singh Center (open to industry, $75-250/tool-hr) and U.S. hybrid HT packaging; no verified U.S. foundry offers AlScN to outsiders.

margin.why: 40-60% on low-volume eval lots, and SBIR Phase III work is often cost-plus.

moat.why: An exclusive Penn/AFRL license would be a real moat, but no license or spin-out was found in two 2026-11 searches.

competition.why: No commercial player found, but unknown AF254-D0806/DV017 performers may already hold the scale-up seat.

regulatory.why: Hypersonics and engine programs mean ITAR/EAR handling; manageable for a U.S. defense buyer.

cycle.why: Completely decoupled from commodity memory pricing.

founder.why: STTR lets a Penn PI carry the research and the founder act as CEO/BD part-time, but a device CTO is required and revenue is past 36 months.

scores.one_line_view: Real physics in a tiny grant-shaped market with no 500C periphery and first sale near month 42: an SBIR mill, not a venture.

tech.why: Parallel F-RAM (FM18W08, RAMXEED MB85R8M2T 8Mbit) ships today; only per-controller card-attribute and timing validation remains.

capital.why: T0: PCB design, East Coast EMS runs and F-RAM inventory fit under $50k.

ttr.why: 6-12 months to first SKUs sold online and to MRO buyers (card 10).

usmfg.why: U.S. EMS assembly of distribution F-RAM (auditor's rubric note: usmfg 3), not U.S.-made memory.

moat.why: Know-how only: open-source DS1230-to-FM18W08 adapters are free on PCBWay, and RAMXEED markets the same battery removal.

competition.why: Memex and Fanuc-card resellers sell battery-backed cards that are mostly out of stock; Everspin parallel MRAM and Infineon nvSRAM are chip-level alternatives.

regulatory.why: Negligible; removing the lithium cell also removes a hazmat shipping issue.

cycle.why: Sold against failing batteries and NVSRAM, not DDR5 $/GB.

founder.why: PCB + firmware + web storefront fits a hardware-curious software builder alongside the day job; may need a contract EE for PCMCIA timing.

scores.one_line_view: A clean, cheap, glut-proof side SKU with a low-$100ks/yr ceiling and no moat: good cash, not a company anyone should raise for.

tech.why: Standard methods on commercial Radiant RT66B / aixACCT testers (P-E, PUND, fatigue, retention, PBTI); TRL 8.

capital.why: High T1: used testers, probe station and parametric analyzer ~$0.3-1M plus a ~$150-180k reliability engineer.

ttr.why: 12-24 months (card 18) to hire, equip and win the first customer from a small pool.

usmfg.why: Lab services near Albany NanoTech or Penn; no manufacturing.

moat.why: ISO 17025 accreditation and customer data help, but the know-how belongs to the hired engineer, and universities own the same testers.

competition.why: No U.S. commercial specialist found (STILL-UNVERIFIED), but Neumonda/Fraunhofer IPMS abroad, Sandia and $75-250/hr university shared tools substitute.

regulatory.why: Mostly negligible; deemed-export and ITAR handling for foreign memory firms and defense primes' wafers.

cycle.why: Startup and VC-funded device demand shrinks in a glut; defense and university work continues.

founder.why: Needs a full-time reliability-engineer cofounder from day one; the founder's ops background fits running the lab.

scores.one_line_view: A labor-bound services shop for maybe 10-30 U.S. customers who can rent the same Radiant tester at a university for $75-250/hr: 38% margins and no scale.

tech.why: MRAM PLP journals ship in IBM FCM3 (128 MB Toggle), FCM4 (1Gb PERSYST, 2024) and FCM5 (2026-10); the kit is integration work.

capital.why: Low T1: contract hardware/FPGA engineer ~$30-60k in year 1 plus boards and parts.

ttr.why: 18-24 months to the first paid design-in after a 6-9-month reference-board build; royalties 30-42 months.

usmfg.why: A reference design; Everspin's 1Gb die uses GF Singapore CMOS with Chandler AZ BEOL, and boards go to any U.S. EMS.

margin.why: 35-45% for years 1-3 because revenue is design services; 60%+ only if royalties appear after year 3.

moat.why: No IP: Phison and Sage already pair controllers with Everspin 1Gb (2019), and Everspin can publish its own reference design.

competition.why: Controller vendors (Phison, Sage, Marvell, Microchip) and in-house teams (IBM) choose the PLP architecture; Teledyne HiRel covers the rugged variant.

regulatory.why: Single-source 1Gb ST-DDR4 faces a possible ITC 337-TA-1487 exclusion order around Jul-2027 (Avalanche v. Everspin).

cycle.why: At $821/GB, MRAM is ~100x the $8.15 glut price, so marginal designs revert to DRAM plus supercaps; the reliability case survives.

founder.why: Founder owns drivers, test tooling and sales but needs a contract EE/FPGA engineer.

scores.one_line_view: Real mechanism in the wrong slot of the value chain: Everspin and the controller vendors own the PLP decision and the margin, so an IP-less kit caps under ~$1M/yr.

tech.why: Lot-specific TID/SEE testing is standard practice (NASA GSFC and ESA guidance); TRL 8.

capital.why: Low T1: ~$100-300k for beam time, delidded boards, a rad-effects engineer and export compliance.

ttr.why: 15-21 months (card 18) to the first paid lot-acceptance campaign after a self-funded seed campaign.

usmfg.why: Services: U.S. beam lines (TAMU/LBNL) and Everspin Chandler AZ parts; nothing manufactured.

margin.why: A heavy-ion campaign costs ~$30-70k against $5-25k reports, and lot-specific RLAT data limits resale.

moat.why: NASA NEPP and ESA ESCIES publish part-type data free, and a non-engineer founder has no radiation-effects reputation.

competition.why: Teledyne HiRel sells screened PERSYST through Everspin's own channel from 4Q-2026; Frontgrade, Honeywell, Avalanche and TRAD R2COTS cover the rest.

regulatory.why: Parts certified to >=500 krad TID fall under ECCN 3A001.a.1, so exports to non-U.S. smallsat builders need licenses; manageable domestically.

cycle.why: Space buyers price on radiation data and heritage, not DDR5 $/GB.

founder.why: The data platform fits the founder, but a rad-effects engineer partner is essential.

scores.one_line_view: Standard practice in a market where NASA/ESA give data away and Teledyne HiRel now sells screened PERSYST through Everspin's own channel; $30-70k beam campaigns leave thin margins for a founder with no rad reputation.

tech.why: Weebit 1T1R ReRAM is JEDEC-qualified in the SkyWater S130 PDK (3 lots, 125C); a 1-4 Mb product needs larger macros, and rad tolerance is 16-kbit gamma data only (TRL 3-4).

capital.why: ~$1.5-3M before production revenue: MPWs, a ~$0.5-0.6M mask set, qualification lots, 2-3 years of an IC designer, plus a Weebit fee (onsemi paid $1.8-2.6M).

ttr.why: Corrected 36 months to production revenue (token samples at 24-30); Weebit's own 12-18-month post-tapeout qualification plus defense design-in puts it at the ceiling.

usmfg.why: SkyWater Bloomington S130 is an open DMEA-trusted foundry under IonQ (closed 2026-07-31), and U.S. OSATs (Integra, Promex) take outside work.

margin.why: 50-65% after the Weebit royalty at $20-200 defense part prices.

moat.why: SkyWater holds a non-exclusive Weebit license, so anyone can build the same chip, and Weebit's first U.S. security licensee may already own the slot.

competition.why: U.S.-made Everspin Toggle ($40M DoW onshore program), Honeywell trusted MRAM, Teledyne HiRel PERSYST, Infineon and Microchip all sell into this socket.

regulatory.why: DMEA/ITAR handling for defense customers is manageable; the rad-tolerant claim may trigger EAR controls.

cycle.why: Defense trusted-NVM demand is unrelated to DRAM pricing.

founder.why: Founder can be CEO/BD, but needs a mixed-signal IC designer cofounder and SBIR money (the SBIR PI rule excludes them while they keep their day job).

scores.one_line_view: The most buildable device card, but a non-exclusive license buys no moat, and a 1-4 Mb ReRAM part loses on density, endurance and heritage to U.S.-made Toggle MRAM at the same ~$3,500-3,800/GB bit cost.

tech.why: Parts exist and Memory Mode/App Direct ship on 2nd/3rd-gen Xeon Scalable; testing uses free ipmctl SMART.

capital.why: T0: a $1-3k Cascade Lake test server plus inventory.

ttr.why: 2-6 months (card 4) to first kits on eBay or a storefront.

usmfg.why: No fabrication; U.S. ITAD sourcing and East Coast testing.

margin.why: 20-35% (mid 28%) on commodity resale with a thin test premium.

moat.why: Used PMem prices are public on eBay ($0.5-3/GB) and ipmctl health checks are free to copy.

competition.why: ITCreations, the Uvation marketplace, many eBay US/DE sellers and ITADs selling direct already list PMem 100/200.

regulatory.why: Resale of used parts must be disclosed as used (FAR 52.246-26 treats used-as-new as counterfeit); otherwise low.

cycle.why: Dies twice: vSphere 8 general support ends 2027-10-11 (VCF 9.0 dropped PMem), then DDR4 falls ~60% as Cascade/Ice Lake fleets retire.

founder.why: T0 software, e-commerce and scripted testing, compatible with the day job.

ttr.why: 4+ years (48 months) for SoC design, AEC/industrial qualification and ecosystem.

regulatory.why: No export issue for edge MCUs; automotive buyers impose AEC-Q100/ISO 26262 compliance.

founder.why: T2/T3 SoC company; card rates founder-doable 'no'.

scores.one_line_view: Head-on against Renesas, ST, Infineon and NXP with a die-area trick that loses to $4 of LPDDR in a glut, fabbed in Dresden: the classic memory-startup graveyard pitch.

tech.why: Pure web software on distributor APIs and PCN feeds; TRL 9.

ttr.why: 6-9 months (card 8) to first paid seats from mid-size industrial OEMs.

moat.why: Cross-reference data is copyable, and the auditor says to floor moat; the DRAM half of the pitch is false (Everspin 1Gb ~$821/GB vs DDR3 ~$25.5/GB).

competition.why: SiliconExpert (Arrow), Z2Data, Accuris, Supplyframe (Siemens) and Octopart/Nexar inside Renesas-owned Altium (since 2024-08-01) already do lifecycle cross-reference.

founder.why: Pure software, part-time-startable; the risk is market size, not execution.

margin.why: IP license and royalty at 80-90% gross margin.

moat.why: A zero-silicon entrant must clear FTO against the RAAAM/Bar-Ilan/EPFL estate; a characterized S130 compiler is the only asset.

tech.why: OpenRAM v1.2.50 (2026-10-27) and the sky130 PDK exist, but only 1-4 KB macros are published and first silicon verified just a 1 KB macro.

capital.why: T0: ~200 hours of contract layout/characterization plus one shuttle slot (~$9,750 in 2021), under $50k total, and paid generation/support starts before silicon.

ttr.why: 9-15 months (card 12); silicon-characterized libraries arrive at ~12-15 months given ~6-month MPW turns.

usmfg.why: Customer silicon is made at SkyWater Bloomington through ChipFoundry or Cadence/SkyWater MPWs; the venture adds U.S. software/services.

competition.why: OpenRAM/UCSC is free and ChipFoundry or Cadence/SkyWater could bundle larger macros, but nobody sells characterized sky130 macros today.

cycle.why: Demand tracks ASIC tapeouts and U.S.-fab policy, not DRAM prices.

founder.why: Python, CI and web tooling fit the founder part-time, but SRAM/EDA characterization needs ~200 hours of contract help.

scores.one_line_view: Founder-doable and cheap with a real gap, but it sits on BSD code in a funnel (ChipFoundry, Cadence, UCSC) that can make it free tomorrow: likely a <$0.5-1M ARR lifestyle business.

tech.why: Async/QDR SRAM is TRL 9 and Cypress built it at Fab 25, but whether outsiders get a characterized high-density 65nm 6T bitcell is STILL-UNVERIFIED, so expect a respin.

capital.why: T2: ~$5-15M for an SRAM design team, 65-90nm masks, a respin and JEDEC/AEC-Q100 qualification.

ttr.why: 30-42 months (card 36) to industrial production revenue; QML/defense design-in adds 12+ months.

usmfg.why: SkyWater Fab 25 Austin is an open 200mm foundry (~400k wafer starts/yr, 65-130nm), but its 65nm SRAM PDK for outsiders is unverified, and the IonQ parent adds capacity-priority risk.

margin.why: 45-60% (mid 52%): ~$2.4 COGS for a 16Mb 65nm die against per-part prices, while undercutting Infineon.

moat.why: A pin-compatible second source has no lock-in until it is designed in; the 15-20-year longevity pledge is a promise, not IP.

competition.why: Infineon is the anchor customer of the same Fab 25, and Renesas EOL260016 (92 codes) maps customers to Infineon parts; ISSI, GSI, Alliance and Rochester also compete.

regulatory.why: Low for industrial SKUs; non-PRC ownership vs Ingenic-owned ISSI is a tailwind, and the rad-tolerant option brings ITAR.

cycle.why: SRAM ASPs are decoupled from DRAM contract prices, and long-lifecycle buyers pay for availability through cycles.

founder.why: Needs an SRAM design team and $5-15M; card rates founder-doable 'no'.

scores.one_line_view: Mature tech at a willing U.S. fab, but Infineon is the anchor customer of the very same Fab 25 and Renesas EOLs funnel straight to it: a $5-15M fight over a shrinking standalone-SRAM pie.
